tools.title: Estimated Tax Safe Harbor Planner
tools.description: Use last year's total tax to estimate a safe-harbor baseline, then build a catch-up plan based on withholding and payments you've already made.
opening: If you have a W-2 plus 1099 income, or your income is lumpy, estimated taxes are rarely a math problem. They are a process problem.
This planner helps you build a conservative safe-harbor baseline from last year's return, then turn it into a clean catch-up plan you can actually execute (with an audit folder that makes sense).

sections.title: How The Planner Works
paragraphs: Step 1 is a baseline: last year's total tax times a safe-harbor percentage (usually 100%, sometimes 110% for higher income).
Step 2 is reality: you subtract withholding and payments already made.
Step 3 is execution: you spread what is left across the number of payments you still plan to make this year.
This does not replace a tax projection. It gives you a defensible floor so you can stop guessing and start tracking.

sections.title: When Safe Harbor Is The Right Move
paragraphs: Use a safe-harbor plan when your income is volatile, your deductions are uncertain, or you are mid-year changing your structure (new S corp, new rental, new business).
The safe-harbor mindset is simple: keep penalties off the table, then do the higher-leverage work (income shaping, documentation, and advisor packet quality).

sections.title: Common Mistakes That Blow Up Estimated Tax
paragraphs: Counting planned deductions that are not executed yet.
Assuming year-end cleanup will fix underpayments when cash flow is already tight.
Treating estimated taxes like a one-time event instead of a system you run every month.

faq.q: Is safe harbor always 100% of last year's tax?
faq.a: Often, yes. Higher-income filers may be subject to a higher safe-harbor percentage. This tool lets you model both so you can pick the more conservative floor.

faq.q: Do I have to make four equal payments?
faq.a: Many people do. If you are behind, the practical move is a catch-up plan over your remaining payments. This tool focuses on execution simplicity.

faq.q: What if my withholding is changing mid-year?
faq.a: Re-run the tool whenever your paycheck changes, you add a side income stream, or you shift profits between entities. Treat it like a monthly check-in.

tools.title: Home Office Reimbursement Calculator
tools.description: Calculate a home office reimbursement amount under an accountable plan using a simple square-foot allocation and a clean documentation checklist.
opening: A home office reimbursement done the right way is not about squeezing every dollar. It is about building a repeatable process your CPA can defend.
This calculator estimates a conservative reimbursement amount using a square-foot allocation, then gives you a documentation checklist so the math actually survives real-world execution.

sections.title: What This Calculator Is Actually Doing
paragraphs: You enter your home's total square footage and your dedicated office square footage to compute a business-use percentage.
Then you add the home expenses you want to reimburse (utilities, internet, rent, insurance, repairs, HOA, and similar).
The calculator allocates each expense by the business-use percentage, then suggests a monthly reimbursement cadence so you can stop doing year-end reconstructions.

sections.title: Execution Notes (Where People Get Burned)
paragraphs: If the space is not exclusive and regular, the math does not matter. The qualification gate matters first.
If you cannot show a simple policy, a reimbursement request, and contemporaneous receipts, your accountant ends up cleaning up a mess at tax time.
Keep it boring: monthly reimbursement, one folder per year, and the same worksheet every month.

sections.title: What To Hand Your CPA
paragraphs: A one-page accountable plan policy (effective date, what is reimbursable, and how reimbursements are requested).
Your square-foot calculation (floor plan or measurement notes, plus photos).
Expense proof (bills, receipts, statements) and a monthly reimbursement log.

faq.q: Is this the same as the home office deduction?
faq.a: No. This is a reimbursement workflow under an accountable plan. The point is a clean, repeatable process and documentation, not a one-off deduction.

faq.q: Do I need an S corp for this to matter?
faq.a: It often shows up in S corp conversations because reimbursements and documentation matter a lot there. The process quality is the real win.

faq.q: Should I reimburse yearly or monthly?
faq.a: Monthly is usually cleaner because it avoids reconstructing a story after the year ends. This tool shows both so you can pick a cadence you will actually follow.

related.label: Augusta Rule vs Home Office Deduction (S corp edge cases)

tools.title: Augusta Rule Rent Calculator + Log
tools.description: Build a clean meeting log, estimate a defensible rent amount, and generate a simple CSV you can put in your audit folder.
opening: Most Augusta Rule problems are not math problems. They are documentation problems.
This tool is built for execution: estimate rent, stay inside the 14-day guardrail, and leave with a meeting log you can hand to your advisor without a long explanation.

sections.title: How To Use This Tool
paragraphs: Add your meeting dates, purpose, and attendees. The tool counts days and builds a simple log.
Enter a daily rate that is defensible for your area (based on comparable rentals or venue costs).
The calculator estimates total rent and flags when you are over 14 days so you do not accidentally convert a clean strategy into a mess.

sections.title: What Makes A Daily Rate Defensible
paragraphs: The rate is not whatever you want. It needs evidence.
Think like an auditor: could you show comps, invoices, or venue pricing that supports the number you used?
If you cannot defend it on paper, lower it and keep the process clean.

sections.title: What Goes In The Audit Folder
paragraphs: Meeting log (dates, attendees, agenda, minutes).
Comparable rate evidence (screenshots, quotes, or listings).
Payment record and entity approval notes (board minutes or consent).

faq.q: What happens if I use more than 14 days?
faq.a: The strategy changes materially once you exceed the guardrail. This tool flags it early so you can adjust before you create downstream problems.

faq.q: Do I need a formal meeting agenda and minutes?
faq.a: If you want the strategy to hold up in the real world, yes. The log, agenda, and minutes are the difference between a clean file and a sloppy story.

faq.q: Can I export this log?
faq.a: Yes. The tool generates a simple CSV so you can store it with your receipts and supporting evidence.

tools.title: Annualized Income Estimated Tax Calculator
tools.description: Turn year-to-date income into an annualized projection, estimate how much you should have paid by now, and build a catch-up plan that matches lumpy 1099 income.
opening: Safe harbor is the simple play. Annualized income is the precision play when your income shows up in waves.
This calculator does not try to be your CPA. It helps you translate year-to-date reality into a payment plan you can execute without panic in Q4.

sections.title: How Annualized Income Works (Plain English)
paragraphs: You tell the tool how many months of income you have so far and what your year-to-date net income looks like.
The tool annualizes that income (projects a full-year number) and applies an estimated effective tax rate.
Then it estimates how much tax should be paid by this point in the year and shows a catch-up plan for the remaining payments.

sections.title: When Annualized Beats Safe Harbor
paragraphs: When you had a slow Q1 and a huge Q3, equal quarterly payments can feel wrong because they are wrong for your cash flow.
Annualized planning matches payments to the timing of income. The tradeoff is complexity and the need to re-run the math when the year changes.

sections.title: Execution Guardrails (So You Do Not Create A Mess)
paragraphs: Run this monthly if you are a 1099 earner. Treat the output like a plan, not a promise.
If you are behind, consider increasing withholding (withholding is treated more favorably for timing) and use estimates only for the remainder.
Keep your calculation printout, assumptions, and profit-and-loss snapshot in an evidence folder for the year.

faq.q: Is this the official IRS annualized installment method?
faq.a: No. It is an execution-first approximation that helps you build a payment plan. For filings, your CPA can apply the official method if it is beneficial.

faq.q: What tax rate should I use?
faq.a: Use a conservative effective rate based on your last return, or ask your CPA for a planning rate. If you pick a rate that is too low, the plan will underfund.

faq.q: Should I just use safe harbor instead?
faq.a: If you want simplicity, yes. If your income is truly lumpy and you want payments to match reality, annualized planning can help.

related.label: Safe Harbor vs Annualized Income (1099 edge cases)

tools.title: REP Status + STR Hours Tracker (Log + CSV)
tools.description: Track hours with categories, produce a clean CSV for your audit folder, and pressure-test whether your documentation is strong enough before you file.
opening: If you want a real estate tax strategy to hold up, you cannot backfill the story in March. You need contemporaneous logs.
This tracker is built like an operator tool: simple categories, fast entry, totals that make sense, and an export you can give your advisor.

sections.title: How To Use The Tracker
paragraphs: Log your date, property (optional), category, and hours. Add a short note that makes the work legible later.
The tool totals your hours, shows category breakdown, and flags missing context (like lots of hours with no notes).
Export the CSV and store it with receipts, calendars, and supporting documents.

sections.title: What Counts As Strong Documentation
paragraphs: A strong log is specific: what you did, where you did it, and why it mattered to operations.
A weak log is vague: a pile of hours with no trail. If your log is weak, your CPA inherits your risk.
Treat this like a monthly system, not a year-end event.

sections.title: Common Failure Modes
paragraphs: Logging big batches of hours on one day without context.
No category mix (everything is just 'management').
No supporting artifacts (emails, invoices, vendor notes, calendar blocks).

faq.q: Does this tool determine whether I qualify?
faq.a: No. It helps you build and export a defensible log and pressure-test the quality of your documentation. Qualification is fact-specific and should be reviewed with your advisor.

faq.q: Should I log travel time?
faq.a: Ask your CPA for your exact rules. The practical standard is: if it is hard to substantiate, do not rely on it.

faq.q: What else should be in the audit folder?
faq.a: Receipts, vendor invoices, calendar entries, property management records, and any contemporaneous communications that support the work described in the log.

tools.title: Cost Segregation Payback Calculator (Sensitivity)
tools.description: Estimate first-year accelerated depreciation tax savings, subtract fees, and see how the result changes under different tax rates and bonus depreciation assumptions.
opening: Cost segregation is not a magic trick. It is an acceleration strategy with execution costs: study fees, documentation standards, and recapture awareness.
This calculator helps you estimate the first-year acceleration signal, then stress test the result under different assumptions so you do not talk yourself into a fantasy.

sections.title: What This Tool Is (And Is Not)
paragraphs: This is a planning model, not tax advice. It estimates a directional first-year benefit based on inputs you control.
The value comes from clarity: if small assumption changes flip the result, you should slow down and get a proper study and CPA review.

sections.title: Inputs That Actually Move The Outcome
paragraphs: Your marginal tax rate (federal plus state) is the lever that converts depreciation into dollars.
The bonus depreciation percentage and the portion of basis reclassified into shorter-lived property are the acceleration engine.
Fees and process quality are the friction. If the packet is sloppy, you pay for a study and still cannot use it cleanly.

sections.title: Execution Notes (Avoid The Obvious Mistakes)
paragraphs: Do not model a benefit you cannot actually use (limitations and passive rules matter).
Keep the study, allocation, and support in one folder and get advisor sign-off before filing.
If you are using this for STR decisions, pair the model with documentation and hours logs. Execution decides the outcome.

faq.q: Why do you ask for my tax rate instead of calculating brackets?
faq.a: Because this is a planning tool. Your real marginal rate depends on your full return. Using a conservative effective rate keeps the model honest.

faq.q: Is this the same as a full cost segregation study?
faq.a: No. A study creates the documentation and the allocations. This tool helps you decide whether the study is even worth pricing out.

faq.q: Does this include recapture?
faq.a: No. Recapture and holding period can matter. Treat this as a first-year acceleration view, not a lifetime optimization model.

tools.title: IRMAA Headroom + Roth Conversion Room Planner
tools.description: Estimate how much conversion room you have before you cross a Medicare IRMAA threshold (using thresholds you enter), then map a conversion plan you can execute.
opening: Most Roth conversion mistakes are not about the Roth. They are about the hidden cliffs around it.
This planner is built for execution: enter your projected MAGI and the next IRMAA threshold you care about, then get a simple conversion headroom number and a plan.

sections.title: How This Planner Works
paragraphs: You enter a projected baseline MAGI for the year (before conversions).
You enter the next IRMAA threshold you want to avoid (thresholds vary by year and filing status).
The tool calculates headroom and shows a conversion plan that stays inside the guardrail.

sections.title: What To Enter So The Output Is Actually Useful
paragraphs: Use a baseline MAGI that is realistic, not optimistic. Underestimating MAGI is how people fall into brackets by accident.
If you are doing QCDs, large capital gains, or one-time income events, model those into baseline MAGI first.
Treat the output as a ceiling, not a goal. You still need a tax projection for full optimization.

sections.title: Execution Notes
paragraphs: Pick a cadence you will follow (monthly or quarterly). A plan that is too complex usually becomes a Q4 scramble.
Save your inputs and a dated projection snapshot in the same folder each year.
If you are close to a threshold, leave buffer room. Small surprises happen.

faq.q: Why do I have to enter the threshold?
faq.a: IRMAA thresholds change by year and filing status. This tool stays evergreen by letting you input the guardrail that applies to you.

faq.q: Does IRMAA use MAGI or taxable income?
faq.a: IRMAA is based on modified AGI concepts. Use a projected MAGI number from your advisor or a conservative planning estimate.

faq.q: Should I always avoid the threshold?
faq.a: Not always. Sometimes the conversion is still worth it. This tool helps you see the headroom and make that decision intentionally.

tools.title: QCD vs Roth Conversion Planner (RMD + IRMAA)
tools.description: Model baseline MAGI, RMD, QCD, and Roth conversions to estimate conversion room before an IRMAA threshold and build a sequencing playbook.
opening: In retirement planning, sequence is often the strategy. Not because sequence changes the math, but because it changes what is possible.
This planner helps you map QCD and Roth conversion decisions against an IRMAA guardrail using numbers you can actually estimate.

sections.title: Sequencing Playbook (What You Are Really Deciding)
paragraphs: QCDs can reduce income from required distributions and create more room for conversions.
Roth conversions can raise MAGI and push you into IRMAA brackets if you do not watch headroom.
The point is to build a plan that fits your reality: RMD needs, donation intent, and bracket control.

sections.title: Inputs That Matter Most
paragraphs: Baseline MAGI (before RMD/QCD/conversions).
RMD amount and planned QCD amount (QCD is limited by RMD mechanics).
The IRMAA threshold you want to treat as a guardrail, plus your buffer.

sections.title: Execution Notes
paragraphs: Do not wait until December to discover you have no headroom.
If you are close to the line, build a buffer and consider using withholding to smooth surprises.
Store the output as part of your year folder so you can explain decisions later.

faq.q: Does the sequence change my tax bill?
faq.a: Often the core math is similar, but sequence changes constraints and guardrails. The practical win is executing a plan without accidental bracket crossings.

faq.q: Can QCD increase my conversion room?
faq.a: It can, depending on your facts. This tool estimates conversion room by subtracting taxable RMD (after QCD) from your IRMAA headroom.

faq.q: Do I need my exact IRMAA brackets for the year?
faq.a: You only need the guardrail you care about. Enter the next threshold and a buffer so the plan stays conservative.

tools.title: Solo 401(k) Loan vs HELOC Calculator
tools.description: Compare payments, interest, and opportunity cost when funding a down payment with a Solo 401(k) loan versus a HELOC (using your inputs).
opening: People argue about which is cheaper. The real question is which is less fragile when reality happens: timeline slips, rates change, or cash flow tightens.
This calculator helps you compare the cash flow and the hidden cost (opportunity cost) so you can pick the tool that matches your risk tolerance.

sections.title: What To Model (So You Do Not Fool Yourself)
paragraphs: The payment you can actually afford matters more than the interest rate you prefer.
Opportunity cost is the hidden lever on retirement-account loans. If markets go up while your money is out, that is a cost.
For HELOCs, rate risk is the hidden lever. Model a higher rate scenario to stress test.

sections.title: Execution Notes
paragraphs: Pick a conservative expected return for opportunity cost. Optimism is how you rationalize bad leverage.
If you are using leverage for a down payment, pair it with a written downside plan and liquidity reserves.
Keep your documentation clean. Lenders and advisors care about the paper trail.

faq.q: Is 401(k) loan interest a real cost?
faq.a: The interest is paid back into the account, but the opportunity cost (missed market returns) can be real. This tool models both.

faq.q: Is HELOC interest deductible?
faq.a: It depends on facts and use. This tool is a cash flow model. Ask your CPA for deductibility rules in your situation.

faq.q: Which is safer?
faq.a: Safety depends on rate volatility, repayment flexibility, and your liquidity buffer. Use the stress inputs to see how fragile each option is for you.

related.label: Solo 401(k) Loan vs HELOC (down payment edge cases)

tools.title: Installment Sale Tax + Cashflow Planner
tools.description: Estimate annual payments, interest, taxable gain portion, and after-tax cash flow for an installment sale using a simple schedule you can share with your advisor.
opening: Installment sales are not just tax strategies. They are cash flow strategies with tax consequences.
This planner helps you map a schedule: what you receive each year, what is taxed as gain, what is taxed as interest, and what net cash flow looks like after estimated taxes.

sections.title: How To Read The Schedule
paragraphs: Each year includes principal and interest. Principal contains a gain portion based on your gross profit percentage.
The gain portion is modeled at a capital gains rate. Interest is modeled at an ordinary income rate.
The schedule is an execution tool: it helps you plan cash and estimated taxes rather than guessing.

sections.title: Common Failure Modes
paragraphs: Modeling the tax but forgetting the buyer risk and collection risk.
No buffer for estimated taxes, then scrambling when cash arrives.
Ignoring how the sale interacts with other income in the same year.

sections.title: What To Hand Your CPA
paragraphs: Sale price, basis, and the proposed payment schedule.
Your assumed tax rates and whether you expect other major income events.
A plan for how you will handle estimated taxes each year of the note.

faq.q: Is this the exact IRS installment sale calculation?
faq.a: It is a simplified planning model. Your CPA will apply the official forms and allocate items based on the final contract details.

faq.q: Does this include state taxes?
faq.a: Yes, if you include state in the rates you enter. This tool uses the rates you provide.

faq.q: Does this replace legal advice on contract terms?
faq.a: No. Buyer risk, security, and enforcement matter. Treat the schedule as the cash and tax layer of a broader exit plan.
